claims.claim_text: Microsoft reports Scope 1 GHG emissions for FY20, FY21, FY22, FY23, and FY24 as 118,100 mtCO₂e, 123,704 mtCO₂e, 139,413 mtCO₂e, 144,960 mtCO₂e, and 143,510 mtCO₂e respectively.

Microsoft reports Scope 2 location-based GHG emissions for FY20, FY21, FY22, FY23, and FY24 as 4,328,916 mtCO₂e, 5,010,667 mtCO₂e, 6,381,250 mtCO₂e, 8,077,403 mtCO₂e, and 9,955,368 mtCO₂e respectively.
Microsoft reports Scope 2 market-based GHG emissions for FY20, FY21, FY22, FY23, and FY24 as 456,119 mtCO₂e, 429,405 mtCO₂e, 288,029 mtCO₂e, 393,134 mtCO₂e, and 259,090 mtCO₂e respectively.
Microsoft reports Scope 3 GHG emissions for FY20, FY21, FY22, FY23, and FY24 as 11,796,000 mtCO₂e, 13,576,000 mtCO₂e, 15,916,000 mtCO₂e, 16,397,000 mtCO₂e, and 15,140,000 mtCO₂e respectively.

Microsoft reports total GHG emissions (Scope 1 + 2 + 3) for FY20, FY21, FY22, FY23, and FY24 as 12,370,000 mtCO₂e, 14,129,000 mtCO₂e, 16,343,000 mtCO₂e, 16,935,000 mtCO₂e, and 15,543,000 mtCO₂e respectively.
Microsoft reports gross emissions net of sustainable fuel certificates and renewable electricity.
claims.source_excerpt: Per the reporting criteria defined in Section 1.10 of this fact sheet, reported values are gross emissions net of sustainable fuel certificates and renewable electricity.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft's Scope 2 emissions include the impact of Sustainable Aviation Fuel Certificates (SAFc) starting from FY23.
claims.source_excerpt: Starting in FY23 reported values include the impact of Sustainable Aviation Fuel Certificates (SAFc).

claims.claim_text: Microsoft's Scope 2 emissions include the impact of both Sustainable Marine Fuel Certificates (SMFc) and SAFc starting from FY24.
claims.source_excerpt: Starting in FY24 reported values include the impact of both Sustainable Marine Fuel Certificates (SMFc) and SAFc.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft has identified partnerships through two leading land protection organizations, the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) within the United States and The Nature Conservancy (TNC) globally.
claims.source_excerpt: Since announcing this commitment in April 2020, Microsoft has identified partnerships through two leading land protection organizations, the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) within the United States and The Nature Conservancy (TNC) globally, to partner with on our land protection journey.

claims.claim_text: A data-informed approach using TNC’s Last Chance Ecosystem Framework and NFWF’s National Landscape Conservation Framework was used to identify ecosystems most at risk.
claims.source_excerpt: A data-informed approach to identify ecosystems most at risk was used, using TNC’s Last Chance Ecosystem Framework and NFWF’s National Landscape Conservation Framework.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft aims to be carbon negative by 2030 and remove from the atmosphere an equivalent amount of all the carbon dioxide our company has emitted either directly or by our electricity consumption since we were founded in 1975.
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft announced in January 2020 that we aim to be carbon negative by 2030 and that by 2050 we aim to remove from the atmosphere an equivalent amount of all the carbon dioxide our company has emitted either directly or by our electricity consumption since we were founded in 1975.

claims.claim_text: We plan to achieve this commitment by reducing our Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions to near zero by increasing energy efficiency, decarbonizing our operations, and reaching 100% direct renewable electricity by 2025.
claims.source_excerpt: We plan to achieve this commitment by reducing our Scope 1 and 2 (market-based) emissions to near zero by increasing energy efficiency, decarbonizing our operations, and reaching 100% direct renewable electricity by 2025.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft’s GHG inventory includes five of the seven GHGs addressed by the Kyoto Protocol—carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft’s GHG inventory includes five of the seven GHGs addressed by the Kyoto Protocol—carbon dioxide (CO2), methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N O), hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), and sulfur hexafluoride (SF6).

claims.claim_text: Microsoft does not currently use or emit perfluorocarbons (PFCs) and nitrogen trifluoride (NF3).
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft does not currently use or emit perfluorocarbons (PFCs) and nitrogen trifluoride (NF3).

claims.claim_text: This carbon inventory reflects what is in scope for our carbon negative commitment.
claims.source_excerpt: This carbon inventory reflects what is in scope for our carbon negative commitment.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft has published the criteria for high-quality carbon dioxide removal: Microsoft Criteria for High-Quality Carbon Dioxide Removal.
claims.source_excerpt: For carbon removal, we have published the criteria we use to help ensure that the carbon removal credits that we contract are high quality: Microsoft Criteria for High-Quality Carbon Dioxide Removal.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft purchases both third-party certified and uncertified tons of carbon removal credits in an effort to develop the market, but only applies the certified tons within its carbon neutrality boundary (Scope 1, Scope 2 market-based, and Scope 3 business air travel).
claims.source_excerpt: We purchase both third-party certified and uncertified tons in an effort to help develop the market, but we only apply the certified tons to the emissions within our carbon neutrality boundary (Scope 1, Scope 2 market-based, and Scope 3 business air travel).

claims.claim_text: Microsoft procures renewable energy from on-site generation, unbundled EACs, PPAs, and green power products.
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft procures renewable energy from on-site generation, unbundled EACs, PPAs, and green power products.

claims.claim_text: Purchased EACs include various types of certificates such as RECs (Green-e certified), guarantees of origin (GOs), renewable energy GOs (REGOs), International RECs (I-RECs), Tradable Instruments for Global Renewables (TIGRs), New Zealand Energy Certificate System (NZECS) certificates, J-Credits, Non-Fossil Fuel Certificates (NFCs), large-scale generation certificates (LGC), Green Electricity Certificates (GECs), Taiwan Renewable Energy Certificates (T-RECs), and PowerPlus.
claims.source_excerpt: Purchased EACs include renewable energy certificates (RECs) (Green-e certified), guarantees of origin (GOs), renewable energy GOs (REGOs), International RECs (I-RECs), Tradable Instruments for Global Renewables (TIGRs), New Zealand Energy Certificate System (NZECS) certificates, J-Credits, Non-Fossil Fuel Certificates (NFCs), large-scale generation certificates (LGC), Green Electricity Certificates (GECs), Taiwan Renewable Energy Certificates (T-RECs), and PowerPlus.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft procures enough renewable electricity to match 100% of its global electricity consumption.
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft procures enough renewable electricity to match 100% of our global electricity consumption.

claims.claim_text: To calculate Scope 2 emissions from a market-based approach, Microsoft captures the impact across all renewable electricity purchases and matches that with the markets where it operates.
claims.source_excerpt: To calculate Scope 2 emissions from a market-based approach, Microsoft captures the impact across all renewable electricity purchases and matches that with the markets where we operate.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft’s water inventory includes withdrawal, consumption, and discharge volumes associated with assets under its operational control.
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft’s water inventory includes withdrawal, consumption, and discharge volumes associated with assets under our operational control.

claims.claim_text: The waste inventory includes the mass of waste generated from operations within Microsoft's operational control that is landfilled, incinerated, recycled, reused, or composted for both non-hazardous and hazardous categories.
claims.source_excerpt: The operational waste inventory includes the mass of waste generated from operations within Microsoft’s operational control that is landfilled, incinerated, recycled, reused, or composted for both non-hazardous and hazardous categories.

claims.claim_text: Microsoft calculates and reports Scope 3 emissions for all relevant categories.
claims.source_excerpt: Microsoft calculates and reports Scope 3 emissions for all relevant categories.
